presentingComplaint: Facial puffiness, dark cola-coloured urine and reduced urine output for 3 days
history: Previously well boy presenting with a 3-day history of periorbital and facial swelling worst on waking, tea/cola-coloured urine, and reduced urine volume. He had an untreated sore throat with fever about 2 weeks ago that resolved. No recent NSAID or new drug use, no rash, no joint pains, no haemoptysis. No prior renal disease. Immunisations up to date. Lives in a semi-urban Indian household.
examination: Alert, mild periorbital and pedal oedema, moderately elevated blood pressure. No rash, no arthritis, no oral ulcers. Chest clear, no crackles at rest; mild bibasal reduced air entry with fluid overload. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly, no ascites. Fundi normal, no papilloedema. Pertinent negatives: no purpura, no haemoptysis, no sinus/ENT bleeding, no features of chronicity (normal growth, no anaemia of chronic disease).

labs.urinalysis: 3+ blood, 2+ protein, dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts on microscopy

imaging: Renal ultrasound: normal-sized kidneys with normal/slightly increased echogenicity, no obstruction or scarring — supports acute rather than chronic process
microbiology: Throat swab negative (post-infectious phase); serology (ASO/anti-DNase B) supports recent streptococcal infection
differentialDiagnoses: Rapidly progressive / crescentic glomerulonephritis (ANCA vasculitis, anti-GBM)
Acute kidney injury of other cause
citations: Harrison 22e — Glomerular Diseases (Acute Nephritic Syndromes / Post-streptococcal Glomerulonephritis)
stewardship: Not applicable — non-infective at presentation. This is a post-infectious immune-mediated process; the antecedent streptococcal infection has already resolved and antibiotics do not alter the course of established nephritis. Management is supportive: salt/fluid restriction, loop diuretics and antihypertensives for volume overload/hypertension.
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, contrast, aminoglycosides) in the setting of AKI
Dose renally-cleared drugs to reduced eGFR
Avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs acutely if AKI/hyperkalaemia present
edgeCases: Persistently low C3 beyond 8-12 weeks or heavy nephrotic-range proteinuria should prompt biopsy and re-evaluation for C3 glomerulopathy or membranoproliferative GN
Rapid rise in creatinine, oliguria and RBC casts may signal a crescentic/RPGN course requiring urgent biopsy and immunosuppression
Can present as hypertensive encephalopathy or acute pulmonary oedema rather than simple oedema
expectedMaiK: Classic acute nephritic syndrome: haematuria with RBC casts, hypertension, oedema and mild renal impairment 1-2 weeks after streptococcal pharyngitis, with low C3 and raised ASO/anti-DNase B strongly favouring post-streptococcal GN. Management is supportive; watch for volume overload, malignant hypertension and any features of a rapidly progressive course.
expectedNextQuestions: Timing and site of the preceding streptococcal infection (throat vs skin) relative to symptom onset
Urine output trend and any features of volume overload (breathlessness, orthopnoea)
Any haemoptysis, rash, joint symptoms or family history suggesting systemic/hereditary GN
expectedInvestigations: Complement levels (C3/C4) and streptococcal serology (ASO, anti-DNase B)
Urine microscopy for dysmorphic RBCs/RBC casts and quantified proteinuria (UPCR)
Renal function/electrolytes and, if atypical or worsening, renal biopsy with ANCA/anti-GBM/ANA

investigations: Urine microscopy (dysmorphic RBCs / RBC casts) and urine protein quantification
Complement (C3/C4) and streptococcal serology (ASO, anti-DNase B)
Renal function panel; renal biopsy if atypical/rapidly progressive

regressionAssertions: stewardship tier must be null (non-infective post-infectious process)
differential must include an alternative renal cause (nephrotic or aki)
